text:
Done. The repository went from zero forAll, zero Gen, zero checkAll to 408 tests including four law families plus verified typeclass laws.

Dependencies: cats-laws and discipline-munit added (neither was present); ScalaCheck was already a declared dependency of every module and had never been used.

Generators (core/src/test/.../Generators.scala): jobId, clusterName, arrayIndex, jobRef, slurmState covering ALL seventeen base states plus Unknown, stateExpression producing the textual forms the CLI actually emits (base, base+flags, trailing-plus truncation), instant, evidenceBundle, acceptanceUncertainty. Shared surface so law families state properties over the real domain rather than a handful of hand-picked values.

Law family 1 — attribution (core/AttributionLawSuite, 6 properties). Operational identity ignores the reported cluster; it distinguishes job number and array index and nothing else; cluster conflict is symmetric; a job never conflicts with itself; an unknown cluster on either side is never a conflict; two known and different clusters always conflict. These pin the rule P8.A1 established after whole-JobRef equality silently discarded every managed observation.

Law family 2 — submission and cancellation uncertainty (ssh/UncertaintyLawSuite, 4 properties). Over every generated failure shape, not the two the hand-written tests use: a disconnect after the request write is never a definite non-submission; the same for cancellation; a disconnect BEFORE the write stays repeatable. The fourth is the one that matters most and was not in the plan — uncertainty must not be INVENTED either. A failure proving non-delivery (AgentUnavailable, AuthenticationFailed, ProtocolViolation, ProtocolMismatch) must stay a repeatable invocation failure, because reporting it as unknown would block retry forever. Both directions of the law are now pinned.

Law family 3 — evidence classification (core/StateLawSuite, 5 properties). Terminality and InterruptionClass are total over SlurmState; ONLY an unrecognized state is Indeterminate; a terminal state is never uninterrupted unless it completed; a requeueing state is never terminal.

Law family 4 — result authority (core/ResultAuthorityLawSuite, 4 properties). ADR 0001 names the validated envelope as authority and denies it to exit zero or stdout; these hold the constructors to that. A failed envelope carries no value that could be read as a result; a succeeded one carries exactly the value given; an envelope is bound to its attempt and epoch; an output manifest admits a path at most once.

Typeclass lawfulness: IdentifierLawSuite uses discipline checkAll on OrderTests for JobId, ClusterName and ArrayIndex — 54 checks. Every identifier ships Order/Eq/Show and -language:strictEquality makes them load-bearing, but no law had ever been verified. A non-transitive Order silently corrupts any sorted structure keyed by these values.

Verification: full suite 408, 0 failed, zero warnings under -Werror. scalafmt clean.

Remaining law families from the plan, not attempted here and still open: journal replay/epoch fencing, atomic publication (partly covered by B3's cross-process suite), batch bijection/sharding, protocol fragmentation and limits. The plan schedules those alongside codec ownership in Phase E.
